parties.ourParty: Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A (Issuer), together with Verizon ABS LLC (Depositor)
parties.counterparty: Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless (as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian)

plans.note: Servicer/Marketing Agent liability and exculpation language customarily sits in Article VI (Servicer and Marketing Agent), with standard-of-care limits in Article III and any general limitation in Article X Miscellaneous. Expect a one-sided liability limitation in favour of Cellco; test whether it caps or excuses breaches of its Servicer Deposit/Acquisition/Representation Obligations, which are our core recourse.

Look for Servicer/Marketing Agent indemnities (Indemnified Person is a defined term) in Article VI, with related obligations of Cellco and the Parent Support Provider in Article IX. Confirm indemnity covers third-party claims and Cellco's own misconduct and that the Issuer/Depositor give no broad reverse indemnity.

A structured-finance TSA does not normally restrict the businesses the Issuer/Depositor may conduct; the only activity limits are the Permitted Activities restrictions self-imposed on the Issuer. Scan Article IX (Other Agreements) and Article VI before concluding absent.

No purchasing exclusivity expected. The nearest analogue is the sole-servicer appointment and the limits on appointing a Successor Servicer (Article VII) plus any covenant in Article IX not to engage other agents; check those before marking absent.

No most-favoured-nation pricing construct in this transaction type; Servicing Fee Rate is fixed. Review Article IX and Article X for any 'no more favourable terms' covenant running against us before concluding absent.

Employee non-solicits are uncommon here, but Article VII (successor servicer transition, where staff transfer is discussed) and Article IX are the only plausible homes; confirm no restriction on our hiring Cellco servicing personnel on a Servicer transition.

Article VII governs Servicer resignation and termination (Servicer Termination Event) and Article VIII governs termination of the Agreement. Key check for us: Cellco should not be able to resign at will mid-term absent a successor and, per the playbook, we should retain termination rights on notice; note interaction with Optional Acquisition/Optional Redemption and Clean-Up Redemption mechanics.

No subscription term or auto-renewal; the Agreement runs until the trust terminates (Article VIII). Confirm no evergreen/renewal mechanic in Article VIII or Article X, then mark missing as inapplicable.

Governing law, submission to jurisdiction and waiver of jury trial should be in Article X Miscellaneous; the dispute resolution / mediation and arbitration provisions (Arbitration Rules, AAA, Requesting Party are defined) sit in Article XI / the Asset Representations Review; Dispute Resolution section. New York is the expected and accepted law; check that arbitration is elective and US-seated.

Expect merger/consolidation and assignment covenants of the Servicer and Marketing Agent in Article VI, general no-assignment language in Article X, and permitted transfers of the Depositor Transferred Property in Article II. Confirm the Issuer/Depositor and the Indenture Trustee may assign or pledge to the Secured Parties and successors without Cellco consent, and that Cellco cannot delegate (Subservicer/Subcontractor) without retaining responsibility.

Ownership sits in the Article II transfer/grant provisions (Depositor Transferred Property, Trust Property, Schedule of Receivables, Receivable Files) and in Article III where the Servicer holds records and Personally Identifiable Information as our agent. Verify records, data and the Schedule of Receivables remain Issuer property and that Cellco takes no ownership interest in our data.

No software/IP licence grant expected; the only candidates are any name/trademark or systems-use permissions in Article IX or the Servicer's use of Receivable Files under Article III/VI. Check for a revocable-at-will licence of Verizon marks or servicing systems before concluding absent.

Regulation AB compliance items (Compliance Statement, Servicing Assessment, Attestation Report, Sarbanes/Annual Certification exhibits) and inspection of Servicer records should be in Article VI, with record-keeping in Article III. Note the direction is inverted: audits here run against Cellco, which benefits us, so do not flag; only check that no audit or inspection right is asserted against the Issuer/Depositor at our cost.

No liquidated damages against us expected. Payment-shortfall and remittance mechanics (Marketing Agent Remittance Obligation, Servicer Deposit Obligation) in Articles IV and VI run in our favour; confirm no penalty, make-whole or fee payable by the Issuer/Depositor on Servicer termination in Article VII.

Representations and warranties of the Depositor and Cellco and the Eligibility Representations sit in Article II, with the reacquisition/acquisition remedy for breach in Section 2.6 (Originators' Reacquisition or Servicer's Acquisition of Bankruptcy Surrendered Receivables) and the Originator Reacquisition Obligation / Servicer Representation Obligation. Assess duration (survival) and whether reacquisition at the Acquisition Amount is a real remedy; also check Article III servicing standard of care.

Insurance covenants are unusual in a TSA; Cellco handles Obligor data as Servicer/Custodian, so scan Article VI (Servicer and Marketing Agent covenants) and Article III (Servicing Procedures, safeguarding of Receivable Files and Personally Identifiable Information) before recording the rule as missing.

No take-or-pay. The closest analogues are the Additional Receivables acquisition mechanics and Acquisition Deposit Amount/Negative Carry funding in Articles II and IV and the Optional Acquisition in Article VIII, all of which are optional or benefit us; confirm no mandatory purchase obligation on the Issuer before marking absent.

Transition assistance and delivery of records should appear in Article VII (Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer) — transfer of Receivable Files, the Schedule of Receivables, data and Collections to the Successor Servicer, plus who bears transition costs (Additional Successor Servicer Fee). Also check Article III record-keeping and Article VIII termination wind-up for return of our data.
